test_title: PYST 24: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - Quant (Held On 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: There are 6 doors. Behind one is a car, and behind the other five are goats. You pick one door. The host, knowing the car's location, then opens 4 of the remaining doors, all revealing goats. You are then offered the opportunity to switch your choice to the one remaining unopened door. What is the probability of winning the car if you decide to switch?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Initial probability of picking the car is 1 out of 6. Probability that the car is behind one of the other 5 doors is 5/6. The host eliminates 4 of those 5 doors, revealing goats. The entire 5/6 probability now concentrates on the single remaining unopened door. Switching to that door gives a 5/6 chance of winning. **∴ The correct answer is 5/6.**
